messages.subject: Number of parameters in model
parts:
Hi all,

I am new to working with Lavaan in R. I am doing a CFA in a sample of N=88. The model I have specified looks like this: 

model <- "
fac1 =~
  item13 +
  item18 +
  item20 +
  item26 +
  item33

fac2 =~
  item3 +
  item14 +
  item19 +
  item24 +
  item27 +
  item32

fac3 =~
  item11 +
  item12 +
  item21 +
  item23 +
  item25 +
  item29
 
fac4 =~
  item1 +
  item4 +
  item5 +
  item7 +
  item9

fac5 =~
  item15 +
  item16 +
  item22 +
  item28 +
  item30 +
  item31 +
  item35 +
  item36

fac6 =~
  item2 +
  item6 +
  item8 +
  item10 +
  item17 +
  item34
"
When looking at the output through summary(model, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized = TRUE) I get that the number of parameters to 123. I got 36 items and each items loading is a parameter in the model, along with each items residual variance and it´s intercept. This accounts for 36x3 parameters = 108. What are the remaining parameters in the specified model above?

When reading other cfa-papers I get confused about the number of parameters reported across the literature. It seems as if the number of parameters one decides to estimate can be adjusted - for instance, does one have to estimate intercepts? These are generally not reported in the literature. 

Thanks in advance!
Adam

messages.author: ff3a366aa7a9b488
messages.subject: Re: Number of parameters in model
parts:
Hi,

Your model contains the following freely estimated parameters: 30 factor loadings, (lambda) + 36 MV residual variances (theta) + 6 LV variances  + 15 LV covariances ( psi) + 36 intercepts (nu) = 123 npar.

If you are unsure which parameters are freely estimated, you can use lavInspect(fit, “free”) or parTable(fit) to get an overview. For example:

library(lavaan)

options(max.print = 999999)

model <- "
fac1 =~ item13 + item18 + item20 + item26 + item33
fac2 =~ item3 + item14 + item19 + item24 + item27 + item32
fac3 =~ item11 + item12 + item21 + item23 + item25 + item29
fac4 =~ item1 + item4 + item5 + item7 + item9
fac5 =~ item15 + item16 + item22 + item28 + item30 + item31 + item35 + item36
fac6 =~ item2 + item6 + item8 + item10 + item17 + item34"

pop.model <- gsub("item", "1 * item", model, fixed = TRUE)
data <- simulateData(pop.model, sample.nobs = 100)

fit <- sem(model, data, meanstructure = TRUE)

lavInspect(fit, "free")
pt <- parTable(fit)
pt[pt$free != 0,]

You don't have to have the intercepts estimated. However, there are situations that require it. For example, for a mean difference comparison.

HTH
